claims.text: OpenAI introduced GPT-5.6-Cyber on August 10, 2026 and made it available through Daybreak Red, while Daybreak Blue provides controlled access to general-purpose frontier models including GPT-5.6 Sol.
OpenAI describes GPT-5.6-Cyber as built on GPT-5.6 Sol and purpose-trained for specialized cybersecurity tasks with reduced refusals for some higher-risk dual-use cyber tasks.
OpenAI reports an internal Advanced Cybersecurity Completion Rate of 95.0% for GPT-5.6-Cyber versus 1.5% for GPT-5.6 Sol and 2.0% with Daybreak Blue access.
OpenAI reports that GPT-5.6-Cyber reaches the High cybersecurity-capability threshold but remains below Critical under its Preparedness Framework.

limitations.text: The benchmark results and real-world vulnerability findings are OpenAI-reported and are not independently reproduced in this Evidence pass.
The controlled-access and authorization context is part of the technical deployment story and must not be omitted when discussing reduced safeguards/refusals.

targets.target: Verify chronology, primary-source identity, technical claims, and overlap before selection.
targets.finding: The OpenAI first-party article directly establishes the August 10 release/access event and provides the product/model descriptions. Evaluation numbers remain vendor claims.

editorial.why_now_note: OpenAI introduced GPT-5.6-Cyber and expanded Daybreak Blue/Red controlled access on August 10 inside W33, creating a distinct model-and-deployment boundary for advanced defensive cyber work.
editorial.rationale: Strong W33 safety/security candidate because the model capability is inseparable from a controlled-access deployment architecture.
